newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen won't sell phone unit stake-report.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen won't sell phone unit stake-report.

text.p: Germany's Thyssen AG no longer wants to sell its share in the E-Plus mobile phone venture in view of increasing growth by the network, a magazine said on Saturday.

The steel and machinery maker and utility Veba AG have broken off talks about Veba expanding its 30.125 percent share in E-Plus by buying Thyssen's share of the same size, Der Spiegel reported in an advance copy of an article due to appear on Monday.
E-Plus, which has trailed far behind the mobile phone units of Deutsche Telekom AG and Mannesmann AG, posted record results and doubled its customer count in the last two months, Der Spiegel said.
As a result, Thyssen chief Dieter Vogel told the company's supervisory board that he was "pleased" with the development and saw "no basis" for selling its E-Plus stake.
BellSouth Corp. of the United States owns 22.5 percent of E-Plus.
